title: Oct 10 Results + Oct 11 Preview: Perfect Start to October Ball
summary: Guardians came through as expected. Now we turn to Milwaukee's home stand.

## October 10 Recap: When Experience Meets Execution

You know, I've been doing this long enough to know that a perfect day doesn't come around often—but when it does, you savor it. The model went 1-0 yesterday, hitting on the Guardians at 53% confidence. Nothing flashy, nothing guaranteed, just solid baseball analysis doing what it's supposed to do.

The Guardians-Sox game played out like a textbook example of home field advantage in October. Cleveland's pitching staff did what they do best—keeping runners off base and making life miserable for opposing hitters. I've seen this script before, and it never gets old when it works.

## Tomorrow's Spotlight: Dodgers-Brewers and the Misiorowski Factor

Now, let's talk about October 11. The model is pointing us toward Milwaukee at 61% confidence, and there's a lot to unpack here. The Brewers get Jacob Misiorowski on the mound at home, facing off against Tarik Skubal—who, let's be honest, has been one of the most dominant arms in baseball this season.

But here's the thing: I've covered enough playoff baseball to know that home cooking matters. American Family Field has been good to Milwaukee, and Misiorowski has shown flashes of brilliance that remind me of young arms I've seen break through in October over the years.

## The Pitching Matchup That Has My Attention

Skubal brings elite stuff—there's no denying that. But the Brewers have been building toward this moment all season. The 61% confidence isn't a coin flip; it's the model recognizing patterns that old-timers like me have seen play out time and again.

Misiorowski at home, October atmosphere, a Brewers lineup that can manufacture runs—these are the ingredients that make for compelling baseball. Will it hit? That's why we play the games. But the edge is there, and in this business, that's all you can ask for.

## The Bottom Line

We're off to a clean start in October, and tomorrow brings another opportunity to let the data do the talking. The Brewers pick isn't a lock—nothing ever is—but it's backed by the kind of analysis that separates informed betting from wild guessing.

Check back tomorrow to see if Milwaukee delivers at home. Until then, enjoy the baseball. October is when legends are made.
